title: Response-time cohort explorer: route & I/O-mode multi-quantile dashboard
creator: Leah Chen
description: Build a reusable dashboard and backing query set that makes it easy for SREs, runtime engineers, and product owners to compare response-time distributions (p50/p95/p99) across models and routing paths, with a first-class breakdown for streaming vs non-streaming I/O modes. The goal is to expose actionable cohorts (request-shape, route, model, streaming=true/false) so teams can quickly identify regression vectors and validate fallback/rollout policies. This ticket covers schema changes to telemetry aggregation, ETS (event tagging) for stream delimiters, dashboard panels, and a small API for automated cohort snapshots used by incident-runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows time-series of p50/p95/p99 for selected model(s) and route(s)
IO-mode toggle (streaming vs non-streaming) filters every panel and updates cohort queries within 2s
Cohort selector supports request-shape bins (short/medium/long), token-count buckets, and stream-fragment count
Backend materialized metrics updated to include 'is_streaming' tag and 'stream_fragment_count' numeric tag
Trace hooks link from any cohort row to a TRACE view with start/end span correlation
Automated snapshot API returns cohort definition + top-10 offending traces for the time window
Performance: dashboard queries return within SLO (99th percentile < 3s) for 30-day windows when using pre-aggregates
Docs: brief runbook added to Confluence describing how to use the cohort explorer in a latency incident
tasks: Design telemetry: add is_streaming bool and stream_fragment_count int to request metrics
Implement ETS tagging in router: mark requests entering streaming runtime and emit fragment increments
Add rollup job: compute daily/hourly p50/p95/p99 by model+route+is_streaming+request_shape buckets
Create dashboard panels: multi-quantile timeseries, cohort table with top trace links, heatmap of quantile deltas
Instrument trace-links: pass trace_id/span_id in cohort query results to open tracing UI
Create snapshot API endpoint and associated permission-checks
Write Confluence runbook + short demo GIF for oncall rotations
Add unit and e2e tests for new telemetry labels and rollup correctness
decisions: Use p50/p95/p99 as primary quantiles to balance noise vs signal for oncall
Add is_streaming as a boolean tag instead of enum to keep query cardinality low
Support request_shape derived from token_count with three buckets: short (<32), medium (32-256), long (>256)
Compute rollups hourly for 30 days and daily thereafter to reduce query cost
Expose trace links only for users with observability:view permission to limit sensitive data exposure
tradeoffs: Adding is_streaming increases cardinality but enables precise breakdowns; mitigated via bucketed rollups
Hourly rollups add storage cost but keep dashboard responsiveness within SLOs for 30-day windows
Trace linking surface is limited to top traces to avoid expensive full-trace expansion in dashboard queries
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoffed with SRE, Runtime, and Console PMs. Agreed on quantiles and request_shape buckets.
2026-02-26: ETS tagging PR merged for router (github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/412). Emits is_streaming and fragment_count metric fields.
2026-03-03: Rollup job prototype implemented in data-pipeline, validated against 14-day backfill. Found mismatch in fragment_count semantics; fixed edge case for truncated streams.
2026-03-08: Dashboard panels implemented in staging console, initial heatmap and cohort table functional. Observability team smoke-tested queries; performance acceptable.
2026-03-10: Snapshot API skeleton reviewed by security; minor auth changes requested. This ticket now exposing UI to internal beta users.
review_feedback: PM (Maya Patel): prefer request_shape labels in UI instead of raw token counts for clarity
SRE (Jonas Meyer): ensure rollups can be backfilled quickly during incident; suggested a backfill CLI command
Design (Ava Martinez): simplify cohort selector to two-step flow to reduce misconfiguration
Security (Priya Shah): restrict snapshot API to service accounts and log snapshot access in audit logs
notes: Next steps after acceptance: instrument alerting on p99 delta > 2x baseline for selected production routes, and add an additional cohort dimension for 'fallback_used' to measure rollback behavior. Consider integrating with Optimize to suggest batching/quantization changes for high-latency cohorts.
